Michael — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. High level response first, details below.

1) Escrow: We can do a third-party escrow for the prepay. Typical setups we see: (A) escrow with quarterly releases tied to committed spend/consumption, or (B) escrow with time-based releases (e.g., 25% at 6 months, 50% at 12 months, remainder at 24 months) + quarterly true-ups. We're attaching a pricing table (v3) showing net effective ARR under each release schedule.

2) Early termination: We propose a refund matrix that diminishes over time and is a function of unused committed dollars minus an administrative/transition fee. We typically cap Redwood liability on termination to the remaining unearned prepay less a 15-30% assessed fee depending on circumstance (force majeure vs. termination for convenience). For M&A/change-of-control carve-outs we can treat that as a negotiated exception; we have a standard change-in-control clause template.

3) Interest on escrow: In our templates interest on escrow accrues to the account holder unless the parties agree otherwise. If Ava wants interest directed to Redwood to offset admin fees, we can do that but it's not default.

Next steps: Rishi will run scenario math (example early-exit refunds under X usage) and Lauren will prepare clean redlines against your standard prepay language so your counsel can review. Can we target Nov 9 for a draft redline so you have time before your Nov 10 procurement meeting?

Michael — adding a quick finance view + sample math so procurement has concrete comparatives. Summary first, details below.

Summary: refunds are easiest to calculate and operationalize when based on unearned committed dollars (prepay balance) rather than attempting to reverse on per-token usage. Usage-based refunds are feasible but require logging reconciliation and additional audit windows; they add ~2-4 week settlement latency. For procurement workflows we typically recommend a hybrid: escrow releases quarterly based on committed capacity (guaranteed availability), with a 90-day post-termination true-up for any usage above committed levels. Refund matrix (example):

- Year 1 termination: refund = remaining unearned prepay * 0.70 (30% admin/ ramp adjustment)
- Year 2 termination: refund = remaining unearned prepay * 0.50
- Year 3 termination: refund = remaining unearned prepay * 0.25

We can make the percentages configurable based on co-terming, prepay size, and whether a change-in-control exception applies. For M&A we usually require documentation (definitive agreement) and offer a negotiated split; we do not automatically treat all acquisitions as automatic refunds.

Attached is a short PDF with the sample calculations and an escrow-term draft for your counsel to review. Note: if Ava wants interest to accrue to the customer, we will include language that requires the escrow agent to credit interest to Ava and provide quarterly statements for audit. Audit documentation: a standard bank statement + escrow agent attestation is sufficient for our internal audit, we do not need the full bank account ledgers.
